status: completed relevance and independent occurrence-evidence review

review.requirement_proposition: Parties must ensure that the information enables affected persons to contest AI-made or substantially AI-informed decisions and, where relevant and appropriate, the system's use itself.

previous_canonical_assessment.applicability_basis: Article 14(2)(b) addresses Parties and their implemented lifecycle duties. The the March 2024–February 2025 Hong Kong bank applications record establishes no entry into force for the relevant Party/territory or implementation approach covering these private actors. Signature and a private company’s AI use do not establish that treaty duty; applicability remains unresolved.

review.reason_for_change: Article 14(2)(b) governs a treaty Party's implementation of transparency/contestability duties. The private perpetrators, companies or bank-verification applications identify no commenced relevant Party implementation/territorial duty.

review.requirement_proposition: Demonstrate that the AI system to be deployed is valid and reliable, and document limits on generalizability beyond its development conditions.

previous_withheld_assessment.applicability_basis: The March 2024–February 2025 bank-account campaign used synthetic facial composites for identity verification; individual application dates are not published. For NIST-AI-100-1 MEASURE 2.5, the missing applicability fact is whether the relevant organisation used NIST AI RMF MEASURE 2.5 for this system’s validity/reliability and limits of generalisation, including the deployment use context; reliance on an output or a performed verification does not establish that voluntary framework undertaking. Taxonomy correspondence does not supply these scope facts; no occurrence-level requirement finding is recorded.

review.reason_for_change: The reported AI-assisted face composites passed remote bank identity checks, directly raising validation/reliability and limits of the consequential verification pathway. The technical bank-control implementation, validation demonstration and documented generalisation limits are unavailable. A successful impostor application is adverse outcome evidence without resolving the full system-validation/documentation proposition.

review.requirement_proposition: Enable assigned overseers, as appropriate and proportionate, to remain aware of the risk of automatically relying or over-relying on system output, particularly where the system informs or recommends human decisions.

previous_canonical_assessment.applicability_basis: Article 14(4)(b) is a Chapter III high-risk-system obligation whose application date falls after the March 2024–February 2025 Hong Kong bank applications. No retroactive high-risk duty or finding is asserted. High-risk classification, Annex III biometric-identification scope and Union nexus are not inferred merely from a hiring or account-opening use.

review.reason_for_change: The registered 2026-07-27 source version (Article 14(4)(b)) postdates the reported application/phishing/transfer/impersonation occurrence. No later report or settlement retrospectively supplies the defined territorial high-risk/prohibition conditions.

review.requirement_proposition: Do not apply affective modeling to identifiable subject data without prior informed consent.

previous_withheld_assessment.applicability_basis: The March 2024–February 2025 bank-account campaign used synthetic facial composites for identity verification; individual application dates are not published. For IEEE-7014 4.3.5.2(d), the missing applicability fact is whether the developer undertook IEEE 7014 for an emulated-empathy system applying affective modelling to identifiable subject affective data; image depiction, face swapping or identity matching does not by itself establish affective modelling, and the anonymous-data exception cannot be resolved without that processing scope. Taxonomy correspondence does not supply these scope facts; no occurrence-level requirement finding is recorded.

review.reason_for_change: 4.3.5.2(d) prohibits unconsented affective modelling of identifiable data. Identity likeness transformation is not evidence of modelling a subject's emotions/affect; the technical subject matter differs.

review.requirement_proposition: For Annex III point 1(a) high-risk AI systems, ensure no deployer action or decision is based on system identification unless at least two competent, trained and authorised natural persons separately verify and confirm that identification.

review.requirement_proposition: AI actors should provide information enabling adversely affected people to challenge AI outputs.

previous_canonical_assessment.applicability_basis: OECD Section 1.3(iv) is used as a nonbinding comparative benchmark for AI actors and affected workplace/identity-decision stakeholders in the March 2024–February 2025 Hong Kong bank applications, not as proof of adoption or a legal duty. The benchmark is confined to the portion of the reported application period after the represented May 2024 revision; individual account dates are unavailable.
previous_canonical_assessment.finding_basis: The sources for the March 2024–February 2025 Hong Kong bank applications establish the occurrence and detection/account-opening sequence, but do not preserve the responsible actor’s complete interaction disclosures, affected-person notices or information enabling challenges. Detection alone is not provision of that information. Neither adequate provision nor its absence is independently proved; the benchmark finding is evidence-insufficient.

review.reason_for_change: Cardholders are adversely affected by AI-composite identity outputs used in bank applications, making information enabling challenge relevant. The OECD 2024 version was published within the March 2024-February 2025 application period, but individual AI-assisted application dates and cardholder notification/review information are unavailable. The post-publication outcome remains Boundary, without assigning syndicate-wide losses to the 15 AI applications.

conclusion_change.previous: Police-sourced reporting establishes that AI face-swapped card portraits passed online checks in 15 account openings, converting a facial-verification result into consequential account-opening authority for someone other than the cardholder. The same reports establish a separate identity-representation failure: the suspects possessed lost cards bearing identifiable portraits and used those portraits as input for unauthorised AI composites. This class covers requester-side misuse; the generator’s private consent controls need not be identified. The financial activity is reported at syndicate level, so no particular loan or card transaction is assigned to the 15 AI-assisted accounts. Police reporting supports the account-opening and unauthorised likeness mechanisms, while subsequent transactions remain unallocated to the AI-assisted subset. OECD challenge information is assessed only as a nonbinding comparative benchmark, and its later version only for the post-May 2024 part of the reported period. Missing information about cardholder notification and review does not establish a breach.
conclusion_change.new: Police-sourced reporting establishes that AI face-swapped card portraits passed online checks in 15 account openings, converting a facial-verification result into consequential account-opening authority for someone other than the cardholder. The same reports establish a separate identity-representation failure: the suspects possessed lost cards bearing identifiable portraits and used those portraits as input for unauthorised AI composites. This class covers requester-side misuse; the generator’s private consent controls need not be identified. The financial activity is reported at syndicate level, so no particular loan or card transaction is assigned to the 15 AI-assisted accounts. Police reporting supports the account-opening and unauthorised likeness mechanisms, while subsequent transactions remain unallocated to the AI-assisted subset. Independent external assessment retains Boundaries for consequential verification reliability/generalisation limits and affected-cardholder challenge information where validation, notification and individual post-publication application dates are unavailable. Different affective/treaty/high-risk objects remain audit-only; no syndicate-wide financial activity is assigned to the AI-assisted subset.
